html:
Utapinõmakãphõná is the self-name of the Tuyuka, an Eastern Tucanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, on the upper Tiquié and Papurí rivers.

They belong to the Vaupés system of peoples who speak different Tucanoan languages and marry outside their own language group, so most people grow up speaking several languages. Neighbours in this system include the Siriano and the Karapana. Catholic missions and rubber collecting reached the area in the 1900s. Today a few hundred Tuyuka live on both sides of the border.
